Docs/Data & replay

Data & replay

Understand the paper's demonstrations, the recorded schema, and the difference between state restoration and action replay.

What the paper reports

The manuscript describes 3,000 replay-successful demonstrations: 100 for each of the 30 canonical stage tasks, recorded at 20 Hz, totaling approximately 9.1 hours. These are paper-reported dataset properties. A public download endpoint or dataset package has not been supplied.

The collection pipeline records simulator state and actions, reviews pending episodes, exports accepted episodes and checks them in a fresh simulator. Offline rendering can produce multiple camera views from the recorded interaction.

Inspect the recorded schema

FeatureRole
observation.stateRobot proprioception and task state; exact width and field layout depend on the task.
actionAbsolute arm and hand joint targets in the collection controller's joint order.
observation.environment_stateFlattened simulator/environment state used for restoration and offline re-rendering.
next.successThe per-step task-success label computed during recording.
episode.seedReset seed used to reconstruct the episode context.

Check the dataset's feature metadata, task/source fingerprint, controller and robot UID before loading it into a trainer. A simulator restoration state is not automatically an appropriate policy input: select the policy's state fields deliberately and preserve the choice in both training and online inference.

Validate restoration and replay separately

  1. Review: inspect the pending episode and its video, including whether the task's physical success condition was reached.
  2. Restoration: load recorded frames into a fresh environment and compare the restored state and observations.
  3. Action replay: restore the recorded initial context, apply the recorded actions open-loop and test whether the task succeeds again.
  4. Export: retain the accepted episode's source metadata, seeds and validation results alongside the training data.

Restoring rigid and articulated state does not restore the solver's transient contact cache. Contact-dependent quantities are excluded from frame-restoration equality checks; a visually similar restored frame does not prove the entire action trajectory will replay successfully.

Run the research validators

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

These examples use a local dataset/session path. The tools inspect and replay existing recordings; prepare the matching runtime and preserve their JSON reports.

python -m data_gen.replay.verify_recording_fidelity \
  /path/to/lerobot-dataset \
  --episodes 1 --stride 4 --action-replay \
  --json-out fidelity.json

python -m data_gen.replay.replay_success_rate \
  /path/to/recording-session \
  --jobs 2 --json-out replay-success.json

Use data_gen/teleop/review_demos.py for review/export and data_gen/render/render_multiview_videos.py for offline rendering. Consult each tool's help and the dataset metadata before scaling up. Keep the raw recordings and validation reports so a later model conversion can be traced to its original data.

Prepare data for a policy

Split data by episode rather than by adjacent frames, record the training/validation episode lists, and fit normalization statistics only on the training split. Preserve camera mappings and any selected state dimensions. Continue with Training & baselines or the teleoperation workflow.
